subject: Order form: requested usage floor & cap adjustment
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@medica.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form: requested usage floor & cap adjustment

Irene — thanks again for the demo. Our CFO reviewed the draft order form and asked us to propose two small changes before we can proceed to legal: 1) a slightly higher monthly minimum (usage floor) for months 4-12 to reflect our ramp profile, and 2) a per-month hard cap to limit overage exposure during peak testing. We attached a marked PDF of the suggested cells (see SOW_ExhibitA_comments.pdf).

Can Redwood confirm if those two adjustments are operationally feasible and whether they trigger any pricing recalculation? We want to avoid an MSA amendment if possible, but we'll accept an order-form level addendum.

Next steps: a short confirmation regarding feasibility and an updated redline so our procurement team can review.

Thanks,
Olivia Grant
Director of Platform, Medica.ai
olivia@medica.ai
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: SOW_ExhibitA_comments.pdf (annotated cells)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@medica.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: requested usage floor & cap adjustment

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and the annotated file. Short answers up front: feasible, and likely yes on a small pricing reconciliation depending on the floor/cap numbers you land on.

Operational notes:
- Usage floor: we can accept a ramped minimum covering months 4–12. This will be implemented as an Exhibit line item tied to billing month.
- Monthly cap: we can enforce a per-month token cap with automatic throttling alerts; overages beyond the cap can either be blocked or billed at an agreed overage rate.

Pricing implications: a floor increase normally reduces unit price in traded discounts; a hard cap that prevents overages may require a modest uplift to the committed unit rate.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) We’ll produce an order-form redline showing the ramped floor + cap options (two flavors: "conservative" and "protective") so you can pick.
2) Karthik will run pricing scenarios and include the delta table.
3) If acceptable, we’ll provide a short cover note for your procurement/legal to show no MSA changes required (order-form amendment only).

I’ve looped in Karthik and Jordan for pricing and DocuSign flow. Expect our redline by EOD tomorrow.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: requested usage floor & cap adjustment — pricing scenarios and redline attached

Team — attaching a quick redline (OrderForm_v3_marked.docx) and a pricing delta table in the header of the document. Summary of scenarios:

1) Conservative (lower floor, soft cap): Minimal floor increase + cap with soft overage (billed at standard overage rate). Delta: +4% on committed unit rate.
2) Protective (higher floor, hard cap-block): Higher floor, system-enforced hard cap that blocks traffic beyond cap. Delta: +9% on committed unit rate, includes reserve buffer for burst handling.

Notes for legal (Marissa): no MSA language changes required; this is an order-form exhibit amendment. Please review the redline for any standard procurement language we should pre-empt (e.g., billing proration for partial months, acceptance criteria references).

Olivia / Medica.ai — Karthik here. I included a short table inside OrderForm_v3_marked.docx with exact monthly floor numbers and resulting unit-rate figures. If you want a hybrid (hard cap for months 4–6 and soft cap after month 7), we can model that — call that Scenario 3 and I’ll send numbers fast.

Jordan — once legal confirms, I’ll prep the DocuSign packet and the HubSpot deal note (RDW-2027-0429).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: OrderForm_v3_marked.docx (redline with pricing table)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medica.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia@medica.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: requested usage floor & cap adjustment

Irene / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed the two scenarios with our finance lead this morning and prefer Scenario 3 (hybrid): hard cap months 1–3 to keep pilot budget contained, then soft cap with overage for months 4–12 and a ramped floor starting month 4. That seems like the best tradeoff.

Olivia asked us to confirm we’re fine with the +6% blended uplift you modeled for the hybrid; we are. Please send the final order-form redline and the DocuSign packet. We need the procurement memo for our legal to sign off; a one-paragraph statement that this is an order-form amendment only (no MSA edits) would be ideal.

DocuSign preference: send to tom.ellis@medica.ai and olivia@medica.ai.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Procurement, Medica.ai
+1 206 555 0124
